involved_tools.name: split_tasks
involved_tools.description:
Break a complex task into prioritized, dependent subtasks and update the task list according to the selected mode. Each task should be independently actionable and verifiable.

Usage rules:
- Provide both required arguments: updateMode and tasksRaw. updateMode must be one of append, overwrite, selective, or clearAllTasks; tasksRaw must be a string containing the structured task list.
- Use clearAllTasks for a new task unrelated to the current list. Use append to retain unfinished tasks and add tasks, overwrite to replace unfinished tasks while retaining completed tasks, or selective to match and update tasks by name while retaining unmatched tasks.
- Keep subtasks to roughly 1–2 working days each, within a single technical domain, and avoid more than 10 at once; if necessary, submit prioritized batches of 6–8.
- Limit each split to 5,000 characters and keep the task tree to at most three levels.
- Make tasks atomic, with clear implementation details and verification criteria. Include dependencies by exact task name and specify input/output and acceptance criteria where relevant.
- For interface-design work, define consistent interfaces, types, required/optional items, errors, naming and dependencies, and useful examples. Provide only high-level pseudocode when needed, not complete source code.
- Ensure tasksRaw is valid JSON content represented as a string; do not include comments and properly escape special characters.

updateMode.description:
任務更新模式選擇：'append'(保留所有現有任務並添加新任務)、'overwrite'(清除所有未完成任務並完全替換，保留已完成任務)、'selective'(智能更新：根據任務名稱匹配更新現有任務，保留不在列表中的任務，推薦用於任務微調)、'clearAllTasks'(清除所有任務並創建備份)。
預設為'clearAllTasks'模式，只有用戶要求變更或修改計劃內容才使用其他模式

involved_tools.name: tasks_setup
involved_tools.description:
Initialize a task source from a file path, creating the file if it does not exist, and return a source ID for subsequent task operations.

Usage rules:
- Call once per conversation when the user asks to use these task tools.
- Ask the user to clarify the file path before calling if it was not provided.
- Provide source_path; workspace is optional and should be the workspace/project directory, such as the IDE-provided path or $PWD.
- Pass the returned source_id to later task tools when possible.

workspace.description: Workspace/project directory path (provided by the IDE or use $PWD)

involved_tools.name: tasks_add
involved_tools.description:
Add one or more tasks in a batch, assigning all of them the required status. Tasks can be inserted at a specified 0-based position or appended by default.

Usage rules:
- Provide texts and status; each non-empty text becomes a task.
- Choose a permitted status based on the user's intent: for example, To Do for upcoming work, In Progress for work being done now, Reminders for ongoing instructions to the AI, or Notes for non-actionable information.
- Provide source_id from tasks_setup when available; if unavailable, ask for a file path and call tasks_setup.
- Set index to a non-negative 0-based position when placement matters; omit it to append tasks at the end.
- Batch multiple tasks in one call when appropriate.

index.description:
0-based index to place the tasks. e.g.:
- 0 for "Do this next"
- Omit to place at the end ("Do this later")

source_id.description:
Source ID from task_setup() response
- Defaults to most recent in the workspace if not provided
- Try to always provide it!
- If you don't have it, ask the user for a file path and call task_setup()

status.description:
You might need to infer it from the context:
- "To Do" for tasks coming up next (e.g. "Do X next")
- "In Progress" for what you'll do now (e.g. "First do X")
- "Reminders" instructions for you (the AI) to be constantly reminded of
- "Notes" to collect non-actionable notes

involved_tools.name: run_sequence
involved_tools.description:
Executes a custom sequence of MCP tool calls. Each step identifies the MCP server and tool to invoke, can include tool parameters, and may declare dependencies on other named steps.

Usage rules:
- Provide the required steps array; each step must include name, mcp, and tool.
- Use name values to identify steps and dependsOn to list step names that a step depends on.
- Include params as an object containing the called tool's parameters when needed.
- Use this tool when you need to specify the tool-call sequence and dependencies directly.
